content.comment_body: I have a [version_no] DC/DC/DC and a [product_name] power unit, plus a modem. [product_name] Power: [article_no] CPU: [article_no] Modem: [article_no] Questions: 1- Can the [product_name] power unit accept either AC or DC (110V) as input? Regarding AC earth, is it possible to connect the AC earth to the DIN rail? 2- The output from the [product_name] power will be connected to x10 as follows: L+: The + from the [product_name] power connects here. M: The - from the [product_name] power connects here. Earth: Connect to the DIN rail (where the AC earth is also connected). 3- When powering the modem, is it possible to supply power directly from the [product_name] power and connect the modem earth to the DIN rail? Alternatively, could the modem be powered from the PLC, and if so, which port should be used—the 24VDC near the x10 interface or from x12? 4- As we will not use any analog or digital inputs/outputs (PLC set as modbus master), can these remain uncabled and without jumpers? Thanks in advance

Search Google for the [article_no] datasheet; you will find many answers. 1- Can the [product_name] power unit accept either AC or DC (110V) as input? Yes. Regarding AC earth, can we connect the AC earth to the DIN rail? Yes. 2- The output from [product_name] power will be connected to x10 as follows: L+: The + from [product_name] power connects here. M: The - from [product_name] power connects here. Yes. Earth: Connect to the DIN rail (where the AC earth is also connected). This power unit features double isolation and therefore does NOT require an earth connection. If desired, you may connect the - of the power unit to the earth of the power supply, but it is generally better NOT to do this. 3- When powering the modem, is it possible to supply power directly from the [product_name] power and connect the modem earth to the DIN rail? Yes, it's possible (not necessary). Alternatively, it can be powered from the PLC, at either the 24VDC port near x10 or at x12 (also not necessary). 4- If you won’t use any analog or digital inputs/outputs (e.g., PLC acts as modbus master), can they be left without cabling or jumpers? If modbus communications are wireless and the power source is a battery, and the modem is wireless (GSM), then no cables are required.
For more details about [product_name] power units, check the following link: [url]. To the right of the [product_name] power unit photo, you'll find ratings for both AC and DC.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are discussing the best practices for connecting a [product_name] power supply with a [version_no] controller and modem. Main points concern input voltage compatibility, grounding procedures due to double isolation, wiring outputs, powering external components, and what to do with unused I/O. The distinction between earth requirements and port selection for auxiliary device power is a common source of confusion.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect clear, step-by-step instructions on how to connect and ground the [product_name] power unit, confirmation of supported input voltages, advice on powering peripheral devices, and reassurance that leaving unused I/O ports unconnected poses no safety risk.
